To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) UHT metamorphism occurred during Ventersdorp magmatism, (2) UHT metamorphic zircon dates peak metamorphic conditions to 2714-2713 Ma and the prograde metamorphic growth to 2720-2721 Ma, and (3) UHT metamorphosed lower crust was emplaced in the upper crust by 2700 Ma.

the UHT lower-crustal granulites record the thermal effects of 2.71 Ga Ventersdorp magmatism, and that these effects were restricted to the central and western portions of the Kaapvaals crust, but not to the mantle keel.

the lower crustal granitic rocks from the Kaapva al craton were subjected to ultrahigh temperatures (UHT) at about 2.72 billion years ago (Ga), and this event was caused by the eruption of flood basalts and the thinning of the lithospheric keel.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the nature and evolution of the deep crust and mantle lithosphere of the Kaapvaol craton, and the processes of crustal melting, metamorphism and magmatism that are associated with the Ventersdor rift.
the nature of the deep crustal processes associated with the generation of the 2.7-2.5 Ga Ventersdorp magmatism and rifting.

the tectonic and magmatic processes that led to the development of the Kaapvaol craton, and the preservation of the ancient diamondiferous lithospheric mantle that is the source of the majority of the world’s diamond production.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the lower crustal UHT metamorphism of the Kaapvaol craton was caused by the Ventersdopf magmatism and rifting.

the lower crustal metamorphic record of the central and southern Kaapvaal preserves a record of the deep crustal thermal response to 2.7-2.8 Ga magmatism, extensional tectonic reworking, and the transient loss of lithospheric mantle thermal support.
the lower crustal granitic xenoliths are a record of the lower crustal metamorphism during rifting and magmation of the Kaapva al craton.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the Kaapva al craton is a "cratonic collage" in that it is the amalgamation of a number of smaller cratonic units, each with its own distinctive history, and each with a different degree of preservation of its original mantle keel.
the Kaapva al Craton was not an unchanging "craton" at the time of Ventersdorp magmatism and rifting.

the UHT metamorphic record of the Kaapva al craton is a manifestation of a transient, non-uniform lithospheric thinness and associated crust-mantle heat advection during the 2.7-2.6 Ga Ventersdorp magmatic event.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Kaapvaol craton has been subjected to a number of extensional events, including the Ventersdor rift, the Bushveld event and more recently the Karoo event.

UHT conditions in lower crustal rocks are a common feature of intracratonic tectonic events, and that the preservation of UHT metamorphic rocks in kimberlite pipes is not a reliable indicator for the preservation of diamond-bearing lithospheric mantle.
UHT metamorphism was a widespread and long-lasting phenomenon that was associated with the Ventersdoprifting event.
